summary: Join our comprehensive training course on Trauma-Informed Care for GBV survivors. Equip yourself with essential tools to foster healing and resilience.
lede: Trauma-Informed Care for Survivors of GBV equips professionals to respond to disclosures with safety, dignity, empathy, and respect for survivor choice. It builds understanding of trauma’s effects on behavior, communication, and trust, helping participants recognize trauma responses and reduce the risk of causing further harm. The course turns trauma-informed principles into practical approaches for communication, environments, procedures, referrals, and case handling. Participants learn to provide confidential, inclusive, survivor-centered support while maintaining appropriate boundaries, accountability, and coordination across services that contribute to protection and justice.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals and practitioners who regularly engage with survivors or at-risk populations, making decisions impacting their safety and wellbeing. This course is designed for: Social workers and case managers supporting GBV survivors. Health care providers such as nurses, clinical officers, doctors, and counselors. NGO and community-based organization staff running GBV, SRH, or protection programs. Police officers, investigators, and first responders handling GBV reports. Prosecutors, legal aid providers, and justice sector actors engaging survivors in legal processes. Shelter, safe house, and crisis center staff. Humanitarian and emergency response staff in camps or displacement settings. Psychosocial support officers and mental health practitioners. Program managers, coordinators, and technical leads overseeing GBV and protection interventions. Any professional who may receive disclosures of violence and needs to respond in a trauma-informed, survivor-centered way.
modules: Recognizing Trauma Responses and Barriers to Disclosure
Working With Specific Groups of Survivors
Legal, Ethical, and Policy Frameworks for GBV Response
Managing Vicarious Trauma, Compassion Fatigue, and Self-Care
Trauma-Informed Practice in Humanitarian and High-Risk Settings
Quality Improvement, Monitoring, and Advocacy for Trauma-Informed GBV Services
prerequisites: Participants should have basic knowledge of GBV dynamics and experience working in related fields. Recommended for those with at least one year of professional experience in GBV, social work, healthcare, or related sectors.
